title.narrative: Mainstreaming an Integrated Water Resources Management Approach for more Resilient Basins in Mozambique

description.narrative: MozWateR (2024–2028), funded by the Netherlands, aims to contribute to water security in Mozambique by strengthening the country’s capacity to effectively implement Integrated Water Resources Management (IWRM) in key river basins in the northern and central water management regions, while also strengthening capacity at the national level. The project is being implemented in collaboration with the Northern Regional Water Administration (ARA-Norte), Central Regional Water Administration (ARA-Centro), and the National Directorate for Water Resources Management (DNGRH) as the main Implementing Partners, addressing key challenges in Mozambique’s water sector. IUCN supports coordinated fund management, strategic planning, organisational development, process improvement, and other high-level project management and coordination functions.

The programme aims to ensure water security and safety for people and ecosystems in Mozambique. To achieve this, the programme objectives include: (i) Investing in human, technical and infrastructural capacity to forecast, manage and reduce the impacts of climate extremes; (ii) Improving the planning and implementation of IWRM interventions; (iii) Creating an enabling environment for sustainable water security and climate resilience; (iv) Strengthening the integration of land and water management, with particular attention to water quality and climate-related risks; (v) Addressing regional imbalances in water infrastructure investment to reduce disparities in access to sufficient and clean water across southern, central and northern Mozambique; (vi) Strengthening the capacity of basin communities, including men, women and youth, to participate in the sustainable use and management of water resources.
